rationale: Overlapping gravidity/parity history counts and the derived binary nulliparity. Nested/threshold representations of the same obstetric history; each member may still carry information the others do not (e.g. losses vs. live births). Co-entry is a modeling-review decision (rank deficiency / VIF within the training process), not a global ban. NOTE on P <-> nulliparity specifically: nulliparity == I(P == 0) is deterministically derived from the parity count P, but it is a NONLINEAR basis function of P, not a linear re-expression -- a logistic-regression design holding P as a count term and I(P == 0) as a binary threshold term can jointly encode a threshold deviation at parity zero and is not necessarily rank-deficient. P and nulliparity are therefore BOTH jointly eligible; their joint entry is a modeling-review / coefficient-stability / nonlinear-basis matter handled within CV, NOT a global hard co-entry pair. Deterministic derivability alone does not justify a permanent co-entry prohibition.
